spec.title: OpenWrt — Operations
spec.description: Single-tabbed OpenWrt operations dashboard for router health, WAN, WiFi, devices, capacity, logs, and optional collectors.

spec.title: Router Health
spec.description: Exporter target reachability. 1 means Prometheus is scraping the OpenWrt router.

spec.title: WAN Health
spec.description: Internet/resolver probes must succeed and internet packet loss must stay below 1%.

spec.expr: (min(openwrt_wan_probe_success{job="openwrt", router=~"$router", target=~"internet|resolver"}) * (max(openwrt_wan_probe_packet_loss_percent{job="openwrt", router=~"$router", target="internet"}) < bool 1)) or vector(0)

spec.title: Online Clients
spec.description: Devices currently marked online by the router textfile collector.

spec.title: Conntrack Used
spec.description: Active conntrack sessions as a percentage of router capacity.

spec.title: Resource Pressure
spec.description: Worst current utilization across memory, conntrack, and overlay flash.

spec.expr: max((1 - (node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"})) or (node_nf_conntrack_entries{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} / node_nf_conntrack_entries_limit{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}) or (openwrt_filesystem_used_percent{job="openwrt", router=~"$router", mount="/overlay"} / 100)) or vector(0)

spec.title: Telemetry Freshness
spec.description: Age of the oldest custom textfile metric. Helpers run on a 1-to-10-minute cadence, so a healthy value climbs to about 10 minutes before the slowest helper refreshes. Yellow past 11 minutes means a slow helper missed a run.

spec.title: WAN Throughput
spec.description: WAN RX/TX bytes per second. Counters are converted with rate() before display.

spec.title: CPU, Memory, and Conntrack Pressure
spec.description: The three fastest limits to check during an incident.

spec.title: WAN Latency & Loss
spec.description: Internet probe latency and loss together, so a slow-vs-lossy WAN is distinguishable at a glance. Loss is drawn on the right as a fraction.

spec.title: Client & Session Trend
spec.description: Online client count and active NAT sessions over time. Divergence (sessions climbing while clients flat) can signal a chatty or misbehaving host.

options.content:
## WAN & Internet
Validate internet reachability first: throughput, packet rate, interface errors, gateway, resolver, and internet probes.

spec.title: WAN Throughput RX/TX
spec.description: Combined WAN throughput for direct RX/TX comparison.

spec.title: WAN Packets/sec
spec.description: WAN packet rate. High PPS with low throughput often means small-packet workloads.

spec.title: WAN Errors & Drops
spec.description: WAN errors and drops. TX drops are included when exported by the node network collector.

spec.title: WAN Probe Packet Loss
spec.description: Packet loss from gateway, resolver, and internet probes. Targets are emitted by the WAN quality helper.

spec.title: WAN Probe Latency
spec.description: Probe latency from the router WAN quality helper.

spec.title: Gateway Packet Loss
spec.description: Current packet loss to the IPv4 default gateway.

spec.title: Probe Success
spec.description: Internet and resolver probe success. 1 means all present probes succeeded.

spec.title: Worst Probe Latency
spec.description: Worst current probe latency from the router WAN quality helper.

spec.title: Internet Packet Loss
spec.description: Current packet loss to the configured internet probe target.

options.content:
## WiFi & Clients
AP-level panels stay low-cardinality. Client MACs appear only in bounded rankings and tables. For dBm, less negative is better: -45 dBm is stronger than -70 dBm.

spec.title: AP Throughput by Band
spec.description: Measured AP interface traffic rate, not PHY/link rate.

spec.title: AP Signal and Noise
spec.description: AP signal/noise from optional WiFi collector. Less negative signal is better.

spec.title: AP Quality
spec.description: AP quality percentage from optional WiFi collector.

spec.title: AP Bitrate
spec.description: AP PHY bitrate. This is link capability, not measured traffic throughput.

spec.title: Clients by AP
spec.description: Neutral ranking of client counts per AP. Higher is not automatically bad.

spec.expr: sum by(vif) (count by(job, router, vif) (hostapd_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}) or (label_replace(wifi_stations{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}, "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) hostapd_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}))

spec.title: Weakest Clients by Signal
spec.description: Bounded bottom-10 WiFi client signal ranking. Less negative values are better.

spec.expr: bottomk(10, max by(station, vif) (hostapd_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} or (label_replace(label_replace(wifi_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) hostapd_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"})))

spec.title: Top Clients by Rate
spec.description: Actual throughput from per-station byte counters when the exporter exposes them (hostapd_stations or wifi_station byte totals). When it does not, this falls back to the negotiated PHY link rate from iw station dump, which reflects link capability, not bytes moved, so an idle client on a fast link can rank high. This exporter build exposes only the link-rate fallback.

spec.expr: topk(10, sum by(station, vif) ((sum by(station, vif) (rate(hostapd_station_receive_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8 or (label_replace(label_replace(rate(wifi_station_receive_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) rate(hostapd_station_receive_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8) or (label_replace(label_replace(wifi_station_receive_kilobits_per_second{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} * 1000, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) (rate(hostapd_station_receive_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8 or label_replace(label_replace(rate(wifi_station_receive_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)"))))) + (sum by(station, vif) (rate(hostapd_station_transmit_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8 or (label_replace(label_replace(rate(wifi_station_transmit_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) rate(hostapd_station_transmit_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8) or (label_replace(label_replace(wifi_station_transmit_kilobits_per_second{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} * 1000, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) (rate(hostapd_station_transmit_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8 or label_replace(label_replace(rate(wifi_station_transmit_bytes_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)")))))))

spec.title: Selected Client Quality Details
spec.description: Bounded operational table for connected WiFi stations. Collector plumbing fields are hidden.

spec.expr: max by(station, vif) (hostapd_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} or (label_replace(label_replace(wifi_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) hostapd_station_signal_dbm{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}))

max by(station, vif) (hostapd_station_connected_seconds_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} or (openwrt_wifi_station_connected_seconds{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} unless on(job, router) hostapd_station_connected_seconds_total{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}))

max by(station, vif) (hostapd_station_inactive_seconds{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} or (label_replace(label_replace(wifi_station_inactive_milliseconds{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"} / 1000, "station", "$1", "mac", "(.+)"), "vif", "$1", "ifname", "(.+)") unless on(job, router) hostapd_station_inactive_seconds{job="openwrt", router=~"$router"}))

options.content:
## LAN, NAT & Devices
Device state, DHCP leases, interface state, and NAT usage. Zero offline devices must render as 0, not No data.

spec.title: Online Devices
spec.description: Online devices from router_device_up.

spec.title: Offline Devices
spec.description: Known devices currently offline. Zero is an explicit healthy zero.

spec.title: DHCP Leases
spec.description: Active DHCP lease records.

spec.title: Conntrack Used
spec.description: NAT/conntrack table utilization.

spec.title: LAN Throughput
spec.description: Measured LAN bridge throughput.

spec.title: Online vs Offline Devices
spec.description: Device count trend with explicit zero-preserving offline count.

spec.title: Top Devices by Traffic Rate
spec.description: Top 10 LAN clients by current combined upload+download rate, from the traffic profile's nftables counters. Empty rather than wrong when the traffic profile is not installed — see Client Insights for a full breakdown.

spec.title: Network Interface State
spec.description: Current interface facts with MAC/broadcast and scrape plumbing hidden by default.

spec.title: All Devices
spec.description: All known devices with online state, hostname/IP/MAC, and no collector plumbing.

spec.title: DHCP Lease Expiry
spec.description: Expiring DHCP leases only. Static/infinite leases exported as 0 are omitted so they do not render as impossible negative durations.

options.content:
## Client Insights
Who is on the network and what they are doing. Per-device upload/download comes from the nftables traffic profile (hostnames from DHCP leases). When the traffic profile is not installed these panels are empty rather than wrong — the device table still lists every known client. Per-remote-destination attribution ("who talked to what") is not sourced from NAT conntrack accounting, which has no cardinality bound; it is deferred to the traffic-attribution phase in docs/client-topology-and-netflow-plan.md.

spec.title: Tracked Clients
spec.description: Distinct client identities currently tracked by the per-device traffic collector.

spec.title: Total Download Rate
spec.description: Aggregate download rate across all tracked clients right now.

spec.title: Total Upload Rate
spec.description: Aggregate upload rate across all tracked clients right now.

spec.title: WiFi Clients
spec.description: Associated WiFi stations across all radios.

spec.title: Top Clients by Download
spec.description: Bounded top-10 clients by current download rate. Descriptive ranking, not a health score.

spec.title: Top Clients by Upload
spec.description: Bounded top-10 clients by current upload rate. Useful for spotting a host pushing data out.

spec.title: Download by Client Over Time
spec.description: Top clients' download rate as a stacked area, so you can see who was busy and when.

spec.title: Download Share by Client
spec.description: Share of current download traffic per client. A single dominant slice is the household's heaviest user right now.

spec.title: Client Activity
spec.description: One row per client, merging download and upload rates with identity from separate queries and a derived Total column. This is a joinByField + calculateField merge, not three separate panels. Clients with no current traffic still appear via the identity query.

spec.title: WiFi Clients by Packet Rate
spec.description: Top WiFi stations by real packet rate from station packet counters (not PHY link rate). Keyed by MAC because the exporter's WiFi MAC casing does not match the DHCP lease map.

spec.title: WiFi Client Detail
spec.description: Per-station WiFi quality: signal, negotiated RX/TX link rate, and session age. The connected-seconds series is label_replaced from station to mac so it joins the signal and rate queries.

options.content:
## DNS & DHCP
dnsmasq resolver and DHCP server health. Cache hit ratio, query mix, DHCP handshake, and pool pressure. All counters are rate-converted; leases and pool sizes are gauges.

spec.title: DNS Cache Hit Ratio
spec.description: Share of DNS queries answered locally from cache versus forwarded upstream. Higher is faster resolution; a sustained low ratio suggests cache pressure or many unique lookups.

spec.title: DNS Queries/sec
spec.description: Total resolver query rate: cache hits plus upstream forwards.

spec.title: DHCP Pool Used
spec.description: Highest DHCP pool utilization across configured interfaces. Approaching 100% means the address pool is nearly exhausted.

spec.title: DHCPv6 / RA Leases
spec.description: Active DHCPv6/RA leases known to odhcpd.

spec.title: DNS Query Breakdown
spec.description: Where DNS answers come from. Unanswered climbing usually means an upstream resolver problem.

spec.title: DNS Cache & DNSSEC
spec.description: Live cache occupancy, stale-cache serves, DNSSEC signature failures, and DNS-over-TCP connection count.

spec.title: DHCP Handshake Rate
spec.description: DORA handshake rates. A healthy lease is Discover→Offer→Request→Ack. Sustained Nak or Decline points to pool exhaustion or address conflicts.

spec.title: DHCP Pool Utilization by Interface
spec.description: Per-interface DHCP pool pressure. Bounded to configured interfaces.

spec.title: DHCP Lease Allocation & Pruning
spec.description: Lease allocation and expiry-pruning rates from dnsmasq, split by IP family.

spec.title: DHCP Pool Capacity
spec.description: Configured pool size, active leases, and utilization per interface, plus static host reservations.

options.content:
## Router Health
Capacity and exporter health. Thresholds are tied to actual utilization or scrape freshness; no decorative limits.

spec.title: CPU Busy
spec.description: CPU busy fraction across all cores.

spec.title: Memory Used
spec.description: Memory utilization using MemAvailable.

spec.title: Overlay Flash Used
spec.description: Writable overlay/rootfs_data utilization.

spec.title: File Descriptors Used
spec.description: Open file descriptor utilization.

spec.title: CPU Usage by Mode
spec.description: CPU time by mode. softirq is normal router packet processing.

spec.title: Load Average
spec.description: System load averages. Compare with router CPU thread count for saturation.

spec.title: Memory Breakdown
spec.description: RAM breakdown. Buffers/cache are generally reclaimable.

spec.title: Conntrack Sessions vs Limit
spec.description: Conntrack active sessions and configured limit. Utilization percentage is shown in the gauges and hero stats.

spec.title: CPU Temperature
spec.description: Temperature from optional thermal/hwmon collectors.

spec.title: Reboots in Range
spec.description: Boot-time changes in the selected time range.

spec.title: Failed Collectors
spec.description: Exporter collectors reporting failure. Zero is explicit.

spec.title: Textfile Age
spec.description: Age of the oldest custom textfile metric. The slowest helpers (filesystem, inodes) run every 10 minutes, so a healthy value cycles up to about 10 minutes; yellow past 11 minutes indicates a genuinely missed run.

spec.title: Router Firmware
spec.description: Firmware and hardware identity without scrape plumbing.

spec.title: WAN Identity
spec.description: WAN IP, public IP, and hostname from this repo's textfile collector.

spec.title: Services Up
spec.description: Count of monitored init services currently running. Compare with the service table below to see which are down.

spec.title: Carrier Flaps in Range
spec.description: Total interface carrier (link up/down) transitions in the selected range. Repeated flaps indicate a bad cable, port, or negotiation problem.

spec.title: TCP Accept-Queue Drops
spec.description: Connections dropped because a listening socket's accept queue overflowed. Non-zero means a local service could not keep up with inbound connections.

spec.title: Softnet Backlog Drops
spec.description: Packets dropped from the per-CPU softirq backlog in range. Non-zero points to CPU saturation on the network receive path.

spec.title: Service Health
spec.description: Per-service running and boot-enabled state from the service-health helper. A service enabled but not running is the interesting case.

spec.title: Firewall Throughput by Chain
spec.description: Traffic passing each firewall chain, from nftables byte counters. A view of where the packet-processing load sits.

options.content:
## Logs & Security
Summary stats use scalar LogQL aggregation. BusyBox cron command-start records can carry error severity while the command exits normally; those records are excluded from error/warning summaries and explained here.

spec.title: Errors (1h)
spec.description: Syslog severity error/critical lines excluding normal BusyBox cron command-start records.

spec.title: Warnings (1h)
spec.description: Syslog warning lines excluding cron command-start noise.

spec.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="openwrt-syslog", router=~"$router", message_severity=~"warning|warn"} !~ "^USER [^ ]+ pid [0-9]+ cmd " [1h])) or vector(0)

spec.title: DHCP Events (1h)
spec.description: DHCP/dnsmasq/odhcpd log events.

spec.title: Firewall Drops (1h)
spec.description: Firewall drop/reject events when firewall logging is enabled.

spec.title: SSH Failures (1h)
spec.description: Precise SSH authentication failure patterns; does not match ordinary 'fails: Exited normally' text.

spec.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="openwrt-syslog", router=~"$router"} |~ "(Failed password|failed password|login failed|Bad password|Invalid user)" [1h])) or vector(0)

spec.title: Total Log Lines (1h)
spec.description: One aggregate count across the Loki stream.

spec.title: Log Rate by Severity
spec.description: Rate of non-cron syslog lines grouped by Alloy syslog severity label. Loki metric queries use Grafana's $__auto interval.

spec.title: Recent System Logs
spec.description: Bounded raw OpenWrt syslog stream. Use Explore for unrestricted investigation.

spec.title: DHCP / DNSMasq / odhcpd
spec.description: Lease assignments, renewals, releases, and DHCPv6/RA activity.

spec.title: Firewall DROP / REJECT
spec.description: Firewall events. Empty is normal unless logging is enabled.

spec.title: Kernel / Driver
spec.description: Kernel, netifd, and link-state events.

spec.title: SSH Security Events
spec.description: SSH authentication and pre-auth close events. Normal '0 fails: Exited normally' cron text is intentionally not classified as failure.

spec.expr: {job="openwrt-syslog", router=~"$router"} |~ "(Failed password|failed password|login failed|Bad password|Invalid user|Connection closed by authenticating user)"

options.content:
## Optional & Diagnostics
Optional collectors live here. Missing metrics render as Not collected/Unavailable instead of green failures or large blank Overview panels.

spec.title: mwan3
spec.description: Availability of optional mwan3 metrics in the selected range.

spec.title: SQM / Cake
spec.description: Availability of optional SQM / Cake metrics in the selected range.

spec.title: nftables
spec.description: Availability of optional nftables metrics in the selected range.

spec.title: IPv6 snmp6
spec.description: Availability of optional IPv6 snmp6 metrics in the selected range.

spec.title: Tailscale
spec.description: Availability of optional Tailscale metrics in the selected range.

spec.title: WiFi Optional
spec.description: Availability of optional WiFi Optional metrics in the selected range.

spec.title: mwan3 Interface Status
spec.description: Optional mwan3 multi-WAN status: one row per interface with a single online/offline cell rather than the raw per-state enum. Empty means mwan3 is not installed or not collected.

spec.title: SQM / Cake Backlog
spec.description: Qdisc backlog bytes from the SQM/helper script. Missing data means tc is unavailable or the helper is not running.

spec.title: SQM / Cake Drops
spec.description: Qdisc drop and overlimit packet rates from the SQM/helper script.

spec.title: nftables Named Counter Rate
spec.description: Bounded named nftables counters only. Avoid source/destination/port-parameterized counters.

spec.title: IPv6 Packets and Discards
spec.description: Optional snmp6 IPv6 counters. Zero discards are normal.

spec.title: Tailscale Interface Throughput
spec.description: Optional VPN interface traffic. Missing data means the configured interface is absent.

spec.title: IPv6 Throughput
spec.description: Router-wide IPv6 byte throughput from snmp6 counters. Zero is normal on IPv4-only WANs.

spec.title: ICMPv6 Message Rate
spec.description: ICMPv6 control-plane activity: RA/ND is normal IPv6 housekeeping; a spike in errors is not.

spec.title: IPv6 WAN & Prefix Health
spec.description: IPv6 WAN reachability, default route, global address count, and delegated-prefix remaining lifetime. All zero means the ISP is not delegating IPv6.

spec.title: UDP6 Errors
spec.description: IPv6 UDP error rates. Sustained receive-buffer errors indicate a socket consumer falling behind.

spec.title: IPv6 Fragmentation & Reassembly
spec.description: IPv6 fragment handling. Reassembly or fragmentation failures point to MTU/PMTUD problems on the path.

spec.title: Metric Inventory
spec.description: Complete Prometheus metric inventory for this job, so every collected series is discoverable from the dashboard itself.
